title: A film’s role determines its requirements
caption: Permanent conductors and insulators serve the circuit; temporary masks and sacrificial films serve the manufacturing sequence.

nodes.label: Conductor
nodes.detail: Carries electrical current in the finished device.

nodes.label: Insulator
nodes.detail: Separates paths that must not conduct together.

nodes.label: Hardmask
nodes.detail: Protects selected material during pattern transfer.

nodes.label: Sacrificial film
nodes.detail: Creates a useful shape or space when removed later.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Transport and reaction determine coverage
caption: Directional arrival can leave shadowed regions; gas-phase transport and surface chemistry offer other ways to coat complex structures. Actual coverage depends on the specific process.

nodes.label: PVD
nodes.detail: Material travels from a physical source toward surfaces.

nodes.label: CVD
nodes.detail: Reacting gases form a film on accessible surfaces.

nodes.label: ALD
nodes.detail: Alternating surface reactions build material cycle by cycle.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: ALD separates the two reactants in time
caption: A surface reaction stops when available sites are consumed. Purges separate precursor exposures; the complete sequence is repeated to build the film.

nodes.label: Precursor A
nodes.detail: React with available surface sites.

nodes.label: Purge
nodes.detail: Remove excess precursor and reaction products.

nodes.label: Precursor B
nodes.detail: React with the surface left by A.

nodes.label: Purge again
nodes.detail: Prepare for the next cycle without mixing feeds.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: The stencil becomes a material profile
caption: Directional removal preserves a different shape from removal that proceeds sideways as well. Mask behavior and surface chemistry influence the final profile.

nodes.label: Protected surface
nodes.detail: Openings identify the regions to remove.

nodes.label: Directional etch
nodes.detail: Removal proceeds mainly downward through the openings.

nodes.label: Lateral removal
nodes.detail: Sideways attack can undercut the mask.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Stop at the right material and depth
caption: Selectivity, endpoint evidence and surface protection work together. Removing the desired layer is not enough if the underlying structure is damaged.

nodes.label: Material selectivity
nodes.detail: Prefer removal of the target over exposed alternatives.

nodes.label: Endpoint signal
nodes.detail: Observe evidence that the intended endpoint is reached.

nodes.label: Profile control
nodes.detail: Manage sidewalls and unwanted lateral attack.

nodes.label: Intended structure
nodes.detail: Reach the target depth while preserving its surroundings.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Place dopants, then make them electrically useful
caption: Implantation introduces selected atoms and damages the lattice. A controlled heat treatment repairs damage and activates dopants within the thermal budget.

nodes.label: Ion beam
nodes.detail: Introduce selected dopant species into exposed regions.

nodes.label: Modified crystal
nodes.detail: The implant profile and crystal damage need control.

nodes.label: Anneal
nodes.detail: Use heat to repair and activate without excessive redistribution.

nodes.label: Electrical region
nodes.detail: The resulting carrier behavior supports the device.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.
